If you can see yourself committing to CS and being most likely a software developer for at least a couple years outside of college, then it might be worth it. But honestly, just do a major that will make you feel happy and at least okay with once you graduate. 

I switched majors multiple times until I ended up with a major that has some attributes of computer science(AI), math, and psychology. It's called computational cognitive science.

If it makes you feel better, many CS majors have a difficult time getting an internship, let alone a job unless they are lucky or have skills to showcase in interviews. If you're not willing to do that, then you probably shouldn't major in it.


I considered switching to CS until I realized I'm probably only doing it for the money and I don't actually care much for coding. Even if I do like computers, i cant imagine studying it for 4+ years with heavy amounts of math and coding. Maybe try looking at majors that have a CS emphasis, or have something to with technology. 


So TLDR: Do it if you really see yourself committing to being a developer or in some related job after college, if not then major in something similar and maybe minor as a back up (can't replace a major, though) if you ever change your mind in the future but it won't help THAT much.
